html:
The Battle of Lake Trasimene was fought on 21 June 217 BCE on the north shore of Lake Trasimene in central Italy. Hannibal ambushed a Roman army and destroyed it, killing the consul Gaius Flaminius.

In the spring Hannibal crossed the Apennines and marched through flooded marshes, where he lost the sight of one eye to infection. He then marched past Flaminius's army toward Rome, burning farms to provoke him. Flaminius followed. Where the road ran along the lakeshore between hills and water, Hannibal hid his army on the slopes. The Romans marched in at dawn through thick mist and were attacked from three sides at once, with no room to form up. Most were killed or driven into the lake; others were captured.

It was the biggest ambush in Roman history. Soon after, Hannibal also wiped out a Roman cavalry force sent to help. In panic, Rome named Quintus Fabius Maximus dictator. He refused to fight pitched battles and wore Hannibal down instead, earning the name Cunctator, "the Delayer". The next year Rome tried open battle again, at Cannae. This was part of the Second Punic War.
